sources.phi: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Chapter 10 (part2 pp. 121-171). Bolts Eq 6.10.168 (p. 130), bearing 10.10.3.10 (p. 132), block shear Eq 6.10.178, welds Eqs 6.10.162-163 (p. 121); concrete bearing φc 0.60 Sec 10.10.8 (p. 137); anchor rods as threaded parts 10.10.9 (p. 138); concentrated forces 10.10.10: flange local bending 0.90 Eq 6.10.185, web local yielding 1.00 Eqs 6.10.186-187, web crippling 0.75 Eqs 6.10.188-189, web sidesway buckling 0.85 Eqs 6.10.190-191, web compression buckling 0.90 Eq 6.10.192, panel zone 0.90 Eqs 6.10.193-196 (pp. 139-144); plate-to-HSS 10.11.1: round 0.90 Eq 6.10.197, uneven load 0.95 Eq 6.10.198, punching 0.95 Eq 6.10.199, sidewall yielding 1.00 Eq 6.10.200, crippling 0.75 Eq 6.10.201, buckling 0.90 Eq 6.10.202 (pp. 147-149); cap plates 1.00 / 0.75 Eqs 6.10.207-208 (pp. 150-151); HSS truss 10.11.2: round plastification 0.90 Eqs 6.10.211, 6.10.213, 6.10.214, T/Y punching 0.95 Eq 6.10.212, rectangular wall plastification 1.00 Eq 6.10.221 (K 0.90 Eq 6.10.228), punching 0.95, sidewall 1.00 / 0.75 / 0.90, branch yielding 0.95 (pp. 153-161); HSS moment 10.11.3: 0.90 / 0.95 round, 1.00 / 0.95 rectangular (pp. 165-170)
sources.hssPunchingRoundK: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.11.2.2.3 Eq 6.10.217 (part2 p. 155): φ 0.90 printed next to Ω 1.58. Ω 1.58 pairs with φ 0.95 elsewhere, so 0.90 looks like a misprint, but it is the printed text and the safe side (owner decision): used for the punching of round gapped K joints only
sources.plateFlexure: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: plate flexure at the bolt line of a fin plate as φ 0.90 Fy Z (BNBC gives no plate flexure rule for connections; consistent with φb 0.90 of Sec 10.6)
sources.boltGrades: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.10.10 (part2 p. 127): Fnt, Fnv of A307, A325, A490 (N: threads in the shear planes, X: excluded) and threaded parts 0.75 Fu / 0.40 Fu / 0.50 Fu
sources.boltAliases: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: ISO property classes 8.8 and 10.9 (stocked in Bangladesh) taken as A325 and A490; Table 6.10.10 lists ASTM grades only
sources.pretension: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.10.9 (part2 p. 125): minimum bolt pretension Tb, kN
sources.holes: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.10.11 (part2 p. 128): standard holes; >= M36 d + 3
sources.netHoleAllowance: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.2.3.13.2 (part2 p. 44): the hole width + 2 mm for net areas
sources.edges: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.10.12 (part2 pp. 128-129); over 36 mm 1.25 d rolled / 1.75 d sheared
sources.maxEdge: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.10.3.5 (part2 p. 129): 12 t, at most 150 mm
sources.longJoint: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.10.10 note [f] (part2 p. 127): bearing-type connections splicing tension members with a bolt pattern longer than 1270 mm along the force: Fnv - 20 %
sources.filletMax: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.10.2.2.2 (part2 p. 116): along edges under 6 mm the thickness, else the thickness - 2 mm
sources.concreteBearing: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.10.8 Eqs 6.10.183-184 (part2 p. 138): Pp = 0.8 f'c A1 (full area), 0.8 f'c A1 √(A2/A1) <= 1.7 f'c A1. 0.8 is printed (AISC 360-05 J8 has 0.85); the printed, lower value is used (owner decision)
sources.anchorRods: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.10.9 (part2 p. 138): anchor rods for the net tension of the base moments, as threaded parts of Table 6.10.10; their concrete anchorage by the anchors table (Appendix K)
sources.methods: SAEngine practice, not BNBC (BNBC requires the effect but gives no method): prying by the T-stub method of the steel design manuals (Sec 10.10.3.6 requires prying in the bolt tension); the elastic method for eccentric bolt groups and weld lines; the Whitmore section (30° spread) and gusset buckling K for gussets; plate flexure φ 0.90 Fy Z; the anchor rod tension of moment bases (Sec 10.10.9 requires it) from a rigid plate on a rectangular bearing block at φc Pp / A1 (method bearingBlock)
sources.bracing: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.19 (part2 pp. 222-227): columns relative Eqs 6.10.285-286, nodal Eqs 6.10.287-288; beams lateral relative Eqs 6.10.289-290, nodal Eqs 6.10.291-292, torsional Eqs 6.10.293-297; φ 0.75; Sec 10.19.4 L/r <= 180
sources.ponding: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 10.16 (part2 pp. 194-195): simplified Eqs 6.10.272-273 (Cp = 504 Ls Lp⁴ / Ip, Cs = 504 S Ls⁴ / Is, trusses and joists Is - 15 %), improved Eqs 6.10.274-275 with Figures 6.10.1 and 6.10.2 (part2 p. 197) digitised at about ±0.01 from the printed curves. The printed figures label their lowest curve 'Cp = 0' (Figure 6.10.1) and 'Cs = 0' (Figure 6.10.2): read here, as the text says, as Cs (Figure 6.10.1) and Cp (Figure 6.10.2)
